Each time one connects, the other is pushed off. The other reconnects a quarter of a second later and pushes the first off in turn, for as long as both stay open, so both screens keep falling back to reconnecting. After this, the newest tab or device keeps the game. The one it replaced stops, says the game is open somewhere else, and offers a Play here button that takes the game back on purpose. Its summary repeats this at `docs/implicit-states.md:167`. - The server closes a replaced seat's socket with the ordinary normal close, with the reason replaced by a new socket: `crates/server/src/actor/match_actor.rs:1691` and `:2118`. The co-op actor does the same at `crates/server/src/duos/actor.rs:1078` and `:1347`. - The client treats that close like any drop: `net.ts:902-937` ends by setting the connection to reconnecting and scheduling the backoff, whose first delay is 250 ms (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS`, `net.ts:96`). `apps/web/src/duos/socket.ts:405` does the same. - A distinct close code cannot disturb a tab's own reconnects. The client already ignores the close of a socket it has replaced itself (`if (socket !== created) return;` at `net.ts:903`; `stale.onclose = null` at `net.ts:362`), so only a socket that another tab or device took over would ever receive the new code. - The client already has the pattern for closes it must not reconnect after: `MATCH_VOIDED_CLOSE_CODE` 4410 and `MATCH_OVER_CLOSE_CODE` 4411 (`crates/server/src/config.rs:879-883`, exported in `apps/web/src/wire/serverConfig.ts:83`). ## Proposal - **Server constant.** Add `SEAT_TAKEN_CLOSE_CODE`, the next free 44xx code, with its reason text, in `crates/server/src/config.rs`, exported to `serverConfig.ts` (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
